entry.title: [BIP Proposal] Anti-Fee-Sniping with LockTime
entry.summary:
The recent updates to the Bitcoin Improvement Proposal (BIP) are aimed at refining the implementation details and enhancing clarity regarding locktime management policies. The draft now explicitly requires that at least one input remains non-final, ensuring that nLockTime is enforced effectively. This adjustment stems from a need to standardize approaches across different implementations, with the current pseudocode suggesting 2**32 - 2 as a conventional choice for sequence numbers.
A new Rationale section has been introduced in the BIP, providing citations to pertinent discussions on GitHub concerning issues related to type flips in locktime ([Issue #26526](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/26526) and [Issue #35628](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/35628)). This addition aims to explain the reasoning behind specific design choices, offering implementers deeper insights into the decision-making process.
Moreover, the BIP now includes guidelines advising that any implementation should thoroughly document its locktime replacement policy, particularly how locktime types are handled across subsequent replacements. This documentation is crucial for maintaining consistency and predictability in transaction behavior under various conditions.
In terms of privacy considerations, the updated BIP emphasizes the importance of maintaining a broad anonymity set as a primary goal. This update is bolstered by references to community-contributed analyses such as the locktime stairs writeup and an unenforced locktime chart, which underscore potential pitfalls in privacy when locktime policies are not properly managed or documented.
Additionally, the draft addresses specific scenarios where the child nLockTime does not safeguard an unconfirmed parent transaction, supporting this exclusion with relevant discussions from the community ([Issue #26527](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/26527)). There's also mention of an ongoing Core Pull Request that aligns with these principles, aiming to establish a minimum height for bump fees to prevent older transactions from being unintentionally prioritized ([PR #36040](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36040)).
These updates are encapsulated in the latest draft available for review at [GitHub repository](https://github.com/nervana21/bips/blob/anti-fee-snipe/bip-anti-fee-sniping-with-locktime.md), which reflects the continuous efforts to refine and clarify the BIP for broader and more effective adoption within the Bitcoin ecosystem.
